A run that declares a concurrency group neither adopts a head nor is implicitly cancelled (reconciled with PAR-152 in code and docs/threads.md §3.1a). Budget: one GET + one conditional PUT issued in a goroutine overlapping the checks mirror/enqueue; zero for dispatches, schedules, PR opened/reopened and any grouped workflow. Tags are a distinct ref: the head key is the full ref, so refs/tags/v1 and refs/heads/v1 never supersede each other (TestTagAndBranchSameShortNameAreIndependent).

Needed from the parser track (T1): carry the raw string in workflow.Concurrency (e.g. CancelInProgressExpr) and pass it through threads.concurrencySpec; threads then evaluates it at creation with the documented context set (github.*/inputs.*/matrix.*), failing run creation on an unresolvable reference. The group half (`${{ }}` in group with vars/inputs/matrix/github) is already resolved at creation (ExpandGroup) and covered by PAR-152's tests.

rows.notes: Wave 2. The group record gained a single `pending` slot: a newer run replaces (cancels) the run already waiting, a live pending run blocks a later run from jumping ahead, the holder's terminal fold clears both slots, and `cancel-in-progress: true` cancels the holder at CREATION (not at the next claim). The run header carries `pending_group` while it waits (cleared when it leaves queued), which the run list and run page render. `queue: single` is this documented model (one running, one pending); a `queue:` key is not parsed and `max` remains PAR-153's cap work. The expression form of cancel-in-progress is PAR-151.

rows.capability: Per-repository and per-organization concurrency caps

A run created above the cap is written with its jobs and pending checks but NOT enqueued, and its header carries hold_reason. A terminal fold releases the oldest held run (one LIST per fold, only when a cap is configured). Admission is a heuristic, not a lock; the reason is always visible. The per-ORGANIZATION cap in this row's capability is not implemented (a follow-up: it needs the org ownership seam); the row turns `have` when it lands.

rows.capability: Schedule operations: next-fire in UI/API, enable/disable without a commit, operator-visible watermark

The sweeper fires at most once per entry per pass and reports Coalesced, never replaying a backlog.

rows.capability: Run prioritization

Priority 0..10 is set only by a manual dispatch (API `priority`, CLI `--priority`); it never bypasses a hold, pause, cap or trust gate. `GET …/api/threads/queue` and `spindle threads queue` show the order.

rows.capability: Queue observability: exactly one named reason per queued job (no runner, labels unmatched, group held, approval, capacity)
rows.acceptance: Every queued job shows exactly one named reason, and the reason changes when the cause clears
rows.notes: Wave 3. Every queued job gets exactly one derived queue_reason (approval / capacity / needs / group / runner availability) in the API and the run page chip. Read-model only; it changes when the cause clears. Runner availability reads the instance registry once per run page.

rows.capability: Per-repository CI pause/resume with in-flight jobs finishing
rows.acceptance: A paused repo claims nothing and resumes cleanly
rows.notes: A per-repository `ci_paused` switch (settings + POST …/api/threads/pause + page toggle, maintain+, audited repo_ci_pause) makes the claim filter refuse the repository; in-flight jobs finish. The marker is mirrored on the queue head so the claim path stays one GET, and every queued job names "CI is paused for this repository". Resume restores claims immediately.

rows.capability: Retention parity: configurable ceiling (≥90 days), keep-forever, separate run/log and artifact windows with artifact expiry defaults
rows.acceptance: A 90-day setting is honoured and reported; an artifact outlives its run only when its own window allows; keep-forever works
rows.notes: Wave 2. Two independent windows: threads.retention (run/logs, default 30d) and threads.artifact_retention (artifacts, default = the run window), each validated 24h…8760h, so a 90-day setting is ordinary and reported (GCResult.RetentionDays/ArtifactDays). An artifact's expiry is its own (upload retention-days else the artifact window) and is NOT bounded by the run: an artifact may outlive its run and is reclaimed by its expiry row. threads.keep_forever skips run/log/artifact reclamation (dead runner records still pruned). The retention-days table in docs/threads.md §3.4 was corrected.

rows.capability: GC parity: expired artifacts, unreferenced blobs, cache eviction, reclaimed bytes per family
rows.acceptance: GC reclaims and reports the bytes it freed per family; a dry run reports the same numbers without deleting
rows.notes: Wave 2. GCResult reports reclaimed bytes per family (run, job, log, artifact, queue, runner) summing to BytesFreed; PlanRetention is a dry run walking the same objects with identical counts/bytes and no deletes (pinned by TestRetentionDryRunMatchesApply). Safety rule: a run is reclaimed only when terminal, past the window AND unattached — any job lease in the future pins it (TestRetentionNeverDeletesAnAttachedRun); idempotent, and the per-repository cadence gate repeats rather than skips after a restart (cmd/spindle/threads_sweep_test.go).

rows.capability: Hosted-label semantics: `ubuntu-latest` (and friends) via a documented operator mapping; `runs-on: {group:, labels:}`
rows.acceptance: A `ubuntu-latest` corpus job runs with zero edits on an instance whose operator mapped the label; an unmapped label queues with a named reason
rows.notes: Landed on main (14cc2f89). ubuntu-latest/ubuntu-24.04|22.04|20.04 expand at enqueue onto the self-hosted + linux set, so an alias still requires every expanded label and cannot widen a runner; windows-*/macos-* stay the D-15 named non-goal. weave/publish-github.yml's ubuntu-latest now schedules.

rows.capability: Label→backend+image mapping (`name:docker://image`, `name:lxc://template`, `name:host`)
rows.acceptance: A runner declaring `ubuntu-latest:docker://node:lts` runs that job in that image
rows.notes: Wave 2. The declared forms are `name:docker://image` (honoured: the job runs in that image when the workflow named no container.image of its own — the workflow's explicit image wins), a plain label, and `lxc://template` / `host` refused BY NAME as the D-15 non-goals. The mapping is stored on the registry record, echoed by register/declare and /admin/runners, and delivered with the job (label_images) while the server applies the selected image to the payload. The label part is still a normal label, so PAR-170's hosted expansion still governs matching: a runner must declare the expanded set too.

rows.capability: Registration scopes: instance, organization, user, repository
rows.acceptance: An org-scoped runner serves only that org and appears in its repositories' lists
rows.notes: The admin-set policy IS the scope: allow_all = instance, an all-`owner/*` list = organization, any `owner/name` = repository (mixed reports repository). RunnerView carries the derived scope/detail. A spindle owner is a user or an organization namespace, so Forgejo's "user" scope is the same owner-namespace shape; there is no separate user-scope credential.

rows.capability: Ephemeral runners: one job, then the record and credential are gone
rows.acceptance: The record is gone after one job and its credential is rejected
rows.notes: `ephemeral` is a runner declaration (register/declare, `--ephemeral`, config file). Capacity must be 1; the runner process exits after its one job, and the server deletes the registry record, credential and token record on the terminal attempt (audited runner_ephemeral_retire), so the credential is a real 401 afterwards.

rows.capability: Managed runner pool (ephemeral, container-backed, autoscaled) so a fresh instance runs queued jobs unattended
rows.acceptance: A fresh spindle boots and a queued job runs unattended inside the documented bounds
rows.notes: Approved non-goal: spindle does not run an autoscaling managed pool (D-14). The documented alternative is scale-out — one-job ephemeral workers (`spindle runner serve --ephemeral`) or capacity-1 runners — under the operator's own supervisor; `spindle runner pool` is a named refusal. A fresh instance runs queued work only when an operator starts a worker, which is the fail-closed default.

rows.capability: Runner groups with org/repo visibility and inherited labels
rows.acceptance: A group's runner is claimable only by allowed repositories, with inherited labels matched
rows.notes: Runner groups are admin-owned records (threads/runner_groups/<id>.json): inherited labels and a visibility allowlist, materialized onto each member runner so the claim path stays one record GET. Group visibility is INTERSECTED with the runner's own policy (a group can only narrow), and inherited labels are unioned for matching. Group CRUD, assignment and membership counts are audited; the JSON API is /api/v1/admin/runner-groups and /admin/runners/{id}/group.

rows.capability: Larger-runner sizing (per-job cpu/memory) or a named queue reason
rows.acceptance: A job asking 4cpu/16GB lands on a matching runner or is queued with that exact reason
rows.notes: A runner may declare `--max-cpus`/`--max-memory` (register/declare fields); a job whose container.options ask for more is not offered to it and the queue reason names the request exactly ("no matching runner offers 4 cpu / 16 GiB"). Undeclared (zero) means the daemon's own limits, so existing fleets are unchanged. The request is a scheduling filter; docker still enforces it.

rows.capability: Stock toolchain images (node/python/go/rust/docker CLI + buildx) published and documented
rows.acceptance: The JS matrix, Go build and docker build corpus rows run on stock images
rows.notes: The documented stock set is the upstream toolchain image per label (node:lts, python:3.13, golang:1.25, rust:1, docker:27-cli, ubuntu:24.04), declared through the existing label→image mapping; `spindle runner images` prints the catalogue and the --labels line. spindle does not publish/mirror those images itself (an air-gapped instance uses --image-prefix), and the corpus-image e2e is not run in this change — the remaining acceptance gap.

rows.capability: Isolation parity: concurrent jobs share no namespace, and the capacity model is documented
rows.acceptance: Two concurrent jobs cannot see each other's processes or volumes; the doc states which setting buys which guarantee
rows.notes: Each job attempt gets a unique deterministic container/network/volume name derived from (repo, run, job, attempt), so concurrent jobs share no namespace and a retried plan is idempotent. The capacity model is documented in docs/threads.md §8.3: capacity 1 is the untrusted default, capacity N is one trust domain for trusted repositories, and a runner that grants privilege or a docker endpoint refuses --allow-fork-runs.

rows.capability: Operator policy knobs: `container.privileged`, `network`, `valid_volumes`, `docker_host`, `runner.timeout` — each with a safe default
rows.acceptance: Each knob exists with a documented default; `privileged` is refused unless the runner opted in
rows.notes: Both halves exist with documented defaults. Limits: threads.retention/artifact_retention 24h…8760h, keep_forever, max_queue_attempts 1…20, job_lease 5m…30m. Container half (runner): --container-privileged, --container-network, --container-valid-volume (repeatable globs) and --docker-host, each validated at startup and re-applied at plan time; the server defers those grantable shapes to the runner, which refuses them by name unless its operator opted in. A granting runner refuses --allow-fork-runs. The /admin/runners "unsafe" marker for a socket/privilege-granted runner is T6 UI work; the runner-side exclusion is enforced here.

rows.capability: Offline registration (config file, no browser) and multi-scope from one process
rows.acceptance: A runner registers from a config file and serves two scopes from one process
rows.notes: `spindle runner serve --config FILE` reads TOML [[runner]] entries — one credential each, so one process serves several scopes — with token_file/register_file (0600 enforced) instead of argv; a literal token is accepted only in the file. The docker/image/container-grant settings are process-wide and shared.

rows.capability: Fleet operations: list/drain/revoke, zero-downtime rotation
rows.acceptance: Draining finishes in-flight jobs and claims nothing new; revocation is a real 401
rows.notes: Fleet operations are list/drain/resume/rotate/deregister/revoke. Drain keeps the credential valid, finishes the current job and claims nothing new; rotate issues a new credential with a 15-minute overlap (the old one is a real 401 afterwards), zero-downtime; deregister deletes record+credential (refused mid-job); revoke stays a real 401. Runner-authenticated verbs (`spindle runner drain/resume/rotate/deregister`) need no admin session; host-admin verbs live at /api/v1/admin/runners and /admin/runners. Every mutation is audited and no token is logged; rotation is shown once.

rows.capability: **Non-goal:** LXC and unisolated host backends; hosted Windows/macOS runners (D-15)
rows.acceptance: The matrix rows carry the non-goal, its reason and the named signatory; a workflow asking for one is a named refusal
rows.notes: Signed non-goal (D-15/S17): LXC and unisolated host backends, hosted Windows/macOS runners, and artifact attestations. Refused by name: runner labels `lxc://`/`host` are declare-time errors; `runs-on: windows-*/macos-*`, `macos-*` and `windows-*` queue with a reason naming the non-goal; `permissions: attestations` was already a named parse refusal; `actions/attest-build-provenance` is a marketplace action refusal. The `NonGoals()` table is the one source the docs, CLI and reason text share.

rows.capability: Log fidelity: `##[group]` folding, per-step timing, whole-run log download (txt/zip), streaming that survives session expiry
rows.acceptance: Grouped logs collapse; a zip download contains every job's log; an expired session reconnects instead of dying

rows.capability: Run graph UI: job DAG with live status, matrix cells grouped under their job, per-step drill-down
rows.acceptance: A matrix run renders one row per cell with its check and duration; the DAG shows blocked dependents

rows.capability: Checks parity: per-check annotations, re-run from the PR panel, per-branch required-check config, check-run API accepting annotations; check-context naming decision recorded
rows.acceptance: An external CI posts annotated checks that gate the merge; the naming decision names the contexts required checks use
rows.notes: Wave 4. The check-run report accepts annotations (error|warning|notice with file/line/col/title, ≤50, bounded and escaped), stores them with the report, and every read returns them; they never change the state the merge gate reads. The PR Checks panel names the Threads run behind the sha and offers re-run to a writer. Per-branch required checks already union require_checks over matching ref rules. Naming decision recorded in docs/threads.md §5.8: Threads contexts are threads/<workflow>/<job>, external CI names its own.

rows.capability: Workflow/runs API and badges (`…/badge.svg`)
rows.acceptance: A README badge reflects the branch's latest conclusion; the API lists/filters runs
rows.notes: Wave 4. GET /{o}/{r}/threads/badge.svg?workflow=&branch= renders the latest run conclusion as an SVG whose state is written as text (passing/failing/running/queued); the read gate is the repository visibility (public answers anonymously). The run API lists and filters runs (workflow/state/branch/event/actor) with cursor pagination.

rows.capability: Run-list filtering parity: branch, event, status, workflow, actor, with pagination
rows.acceptance: The documented filter set narrows the list correctly, and the page stays usable at 390 px
rows.notes: Wave 4. The documented filter set (workflow, state, branch, event, actor) narrows the API and the page from one bounded scan (filterScanMax = 1000 headers per page, `more` says the bound was hit). The page form is a plain GET at 2-up/3-up/6-up grid so it stays usable at 390 px.

rows.capability: Cancel/rerun granularity: whole run, single job, force-cancel, and a "cancelled by X" record
rows.acceptance: Cancelling one job leaves its siblings running; the record names the actor
rows.notes: Wave 4. POST …/{run}/jobs/{job}/cancel (optional force) cancels exactly one job; siblings keep running. Non-force running attempts get the cancel signal and end on ack; force is terminal at once and a later complete is a 409. The job records cancelled_by/cancel_reason/force_cancelled and the first cancel wins. The page renders both controls and the actor; the run verb remains the whole-run path.

rows.capability: Authoring affordances: validate-on-save with key-level errors, schema-assisted editor
rows.acceptance: An invalid key is reported in the editor, not only after a push; the message names key and file
rows.notes: `POST …/api/threads/validate` runs the same parser a push uses and maps yaml errors to YAML key paths and lines (`jobs.build.bogus-key`, line 5), naming the file; the Threads page has an editor pane with a validate button and the key-level result. `spindle threads explain FILE` summarises triggers/jobs/runs-on/needs locally. Nothing is stored or executed.

rows.capability: Notifications parity: failure notifications (UI/webhook/email) and per-user workflow subscriptions
rows.acceptance: A failed watched workflow notifies its subscribers once, with the run link
rows.notes: A signed-in user can watch a repository (or named workflows); a failed run writes exactly ONE durable in-app notification per (user, run) with the run link, and an optional repository `notify_webhook` receives one POST with the same facts (no redirects, 5s timeout). Email is not implemented because this instance runs no mailer — named in docs/threads.md §9 rather than an inert control; that is the remaining acceptance gap.

rows.capability: CLI parity: `threads run --ref` with inputs, `threads watch`, run/job listing
rows.acceptance: The CLI dispatches with inputs and follows the run to completion; exit codes match the API
rows.notes: CLI parity: `threads run --ref` accepts repeatable `--input k=v` and `--priority`, `threads watch` follows the run and exits 0 success / 1 failure / 130 cancelled, `threads jobs` lists a run, and schedule/pause/resume/queue/explain are present. Exit codes match the API (a 404 is exit 3 via the shared client).

rows.capability: `spindle threads validate` offline validation with the same errors the server reports
rows.acceptance: A file validates offline with byte-identical error text to the server for a table of bad files
rows.notes: Landed (Wave 5). `spindle threads validate [PATH|-] [--repo DIR] [--json]` is operator-local and runs `threads.ValidateWorkflowSource` — the same parser/validator the push path and the authoring pane use — so error text is byte-identical to the server's (pin: TestThreadsValidateMatchesTheServerErrorText over a bad-file table). PATH is a file, a directory of direct *.yml/*.yaml children, or `-` for stdin; `--repo DIR` validates DIR/.spindle/workflows. Human output is `file:line: key: message`; `--json` returns the server's WorkflowValidation shape. Exit 0 valid, 1 invalid/unreadable, 2 usage. `threads explain` is unchanged and shares the parser, not the output.

rows.capability: Conformance corpus + harness (`internal/e2e/parity_test.go`, `testdata/parity/{forgejo,github}`) driven through discovery → run → checks → artifacts
rows.acceptance: `make parity` runs the corpus; a deliberately broken row makes it fail; a Forgejo corpus entry runs unmodified after conversion
rows.notes: Wave 1d: the corpus (the four Weave/Scriobh Forgejo files), the SOURCE stamps, the importer-produced goldens and the parse/plan + trigger tiers are committed and run in -short. After the 1a/1b/1c/importer/tag merges ALL FOUR convert, parse and plan with zero UNTRANSLATED constructs, and scriobh-release keeps its four matrix cells; the tags-only file is driven by a tag and does not fire on a branch. The execution tier (a real runner + docker) is opt-in (SPINDLE_PARITY_EXEC=1, make parity-exec). Still partial on the plan's definition: the corpus does not yet RUN unmodified end to end (images, network, a runner), and the GitHub half waits on a GitHub-side corpus with converted goldens.

rows.capability: `make parity` gate: no `missing` row, no `partial` without a wave or decision, no `have` row without an existing, passing named test
rows.acceptance: Removing a named test from the tree fails the gate with the row id; adding a row without a test fails
rows.notes: Wave 1d. `make parity` runs the gate and the corpus parse tier; CI runs it in the gate job (no docker). `make parity-closed` adds the plan's §9 closure rule (no missing row) — a separate mode because Wave 1 lands with later waves still missing by design.

rows.capability: Living matrix (`docs/features/parity/parity.json` + generated `matrix.md`) with the docs-revision stamp; docs drift corrected
rows.acceptance: Every `PAR-` id appears once; the stamp names both docs revisions; `docs/threads.md` §11 matches §5.5/§5.6 and `15_threads.md` §2.6/§2.7
rows.notes: Wave 1d. docs/features/parity/parity.json holds all 119 plan rows with the docs-revision stamp; matrix.md is generated by internal/devtools/paritygate and the gate fails a stale or hand-edited copy. The plan's finding that docs/threads.md §11 still claimed "no OIDC / no environments" is no longer true at this baseline (the §11 rewrite landed in 3491c8a7); §11 was re-read against §5.5/§5.6 and 15_threads.md §2.6/§2.7 in this change.
